text: On 2 April 2003 a regional hospital in southern Ontario closed its emergency department and suspended elective surgery after a patient admitted with pneumonia was classed as a probable case of SARS. Two nurses and a respiratory therapist who had cared for him developed fever within the week. More than 300 staff were placed in work quarantine, travelling only between home and the hospital and wearing N95 masks at all times, and about 900 visitors and outpatients were asked to stay home for ten days. Screening desks were set up at every entrance. No further spread was found, and the hospital reopened to visitors at the end of the month.
label: epidemic

text: GLACE BAY, N.S., autumn 1924 - Diphtheria has now claimed 14 lives in the mining town, with 112 cases reported; antitoxin was rushed from Halifax by train.
label: epidemic

text: An outbreak of COVID-19 in a remote Dene community in the Northwest Territories in the fall of 2021 infected more than 90 people out of a population of about 700 in two weeks. The territory sent a rapid response team of nurses and set up an isolation site in the community hall. Food hampers were delivered to households in isolation. Three elders were flown to Yellowknife, and one died.
label: epidemic

text: HALIFAX, Aug. 2, 1910 - The steamer Lakonia, from Naples with 600 Italian immigrants, has been held at the quarantine station at McNabs Island after one of the steerage passengers died at sea of a disease which the port physician believes to be cholera. Eight more are ill. The steerage is being fumigated and no person will be allowed ashore until the disease has run its course. A cordon of police boats patrols the anchorage.
label: epidemic

text: Influenza swept through a logging camp on the upper Gatineau in January 1926, laying up 70 of the 110 men. With the thermometer at 40 below, the camp boss sent a team to Maniwaki for a doctor, who arrived after two days on the road. Four men died of pneumonia.
label: epidemic

text: BRANTFORD, Ont., Sept. 1934 - The medical officer of health has traced the outbreak of typhoid fever in the city to raw milk from a dairy farm in the township, where a farmhand was found to be a carrier of the disease. Forty-three people have been taken ill, and three have died. The dairy's licence has been suspended, and the board of health is urging the council to require that all milk sold in the city be pasteurized.
label: epidemic

text: Meningococcal disease, Edmonton high school, March 2006: four students ill, one died. More than 1,200 students and staff given antibiotics and vaccine at a clinic in the gym.
label: epidemic

text: The poliomyelitis epidemic of the summer of 1947 struck the towns of the British Columbia interior with particular severity. Vernon, Kamloops and Penticton between them reported 86 cases by the middle of September, and nine deaths. Respirators were flown in from Vancouver, and an old army hut at Kamloops was fitted up as an emergency ward. Swimming in the lakes was forbidden, the summer fairs were cancelled and Sunday schools stayed closed. Fear of the disease kept many families from travelling; motor courts along the highway reported their worst season in years.
label: epidemic

text: A rural Alberta county recorded 140 confirmed cases of pertussis in 2015, mostly children who were not fully immunized; two infants were hospitalized.
label: epidemic

text: Cryptosporidiosis outbreak, municipal wave pool in a Prairie city, July 2007: about 250 ill with watery diarrhea. Pool closed and super-chlorinated.
label: epidemic

text: A shigellosis outbreak in a fly-in community in northern Manitoba during the summer of 1987 affected more than 130 people, about a fifth of the population, most of them young children. Homes without running water or sewage disposal made it nearly impossible to stop the spread. Nurses handed out antibiotics and soap and gave classes on handwashing, and the federal government sent water trucks.
label: epidemic

text: YARMOUTH, N.S., March 1915 - La grippe is unusually prevalent in this town and county. The doctors are run off their feet, and in some families every member is down at once. The Academy has been closed for a week, as half the pupils and two of the teachers are ill.
label: epidemic

text: Five members of an extended family in a Nunavik village were flown to Montreal in July 1993 with botulism after eating fermented seal flipper that had been stored in a plastic container rather than in the traditional way. Two needed mechanical ventilation for several weeks. Health officials visited every household to explain the risk and distributed antitoxin to the nursing station.
label: epidemic

text: Typhoid fever has been epidemic at Lethbridge since the middle of August 1919, when the long drought left the river so low that the town intake drew water from stagnant pools along the bank. There have been 64 cases and five deaths. The provincial laboratory found the water heavily contaminated, and chlorination has been started. People are warned to boil all water and milk.
label: epidemic

text: More than 900 cases of measles were reported in Saint John, N.B., in two months of 1937, and eleven small children died.
label: epidemic

text: A cruise ship arrived in Halifax in September 2016 with 160 passengers and crew sick with norovirus; the ill were kept aboard and the ship was disinfected before sailing.
label: epidemic

text: About two thousand people who fled a forest fire in northern Saskatchewan in July 1995 were housed in arenas and school gymnasiums in Prince Albert. Within days a gastrointestinal illness spread through the crowded shelters, and 280 evacuees were seen by nurses for vomiting and diarrhea. Public health staff added portable washrooms and handwashing stations, moved the sickest people to separate rooms and stopped communal meals in favour of boxed lunches. Norovirus was later confirmed in stool samples.
label: epidemic

text: The board of health made vaccination compulsory for school children after 28 cases of smallpox, all in unvaccinated persons, appeared in Niagara Falls, Ont., in the spring of 1927.
label: epidemic

text: Infectious disease report, autumn 1977: an outbreak of measles in a Manitoba school division infected 97 children aged 5 to 15. Most of the children had never been vaccinated. Three were admitted to hospital, one with pneumonia and two with encephalitis.
label: epidemic

text: Influenza at a mining camp near Kirkland Lake, December 1921: eighty men down, three deaths, and the mill shut for a week for want of hands.
label: epidemic

text: The epidemic of scarlet fever at the city of Moose Jaw, which began in January 1941, has reached 216 cases. Two children have died. The isolation hospital is full, and the medical health officer has ordered that all children in a household where a case occurs be kept out of school for three weeks, with the house placarded. Milk delivery men have been told not to enter kitchens.
label: epidemic

text: An outbreak of whooping cough at a rural Mennonite community near Steinbach, winter 1958: 54 cases, one infant death.
label: epidemic

text: In March 2009, health officials in a northern British Columbia town declared an outbreak of tuberculosis after seven cases were diagnosed in three months among people who frequented the same bar and rooming house. Public health nurses went out with mobile x-ray equipment and tested 420 contacts.
label: epidemic

text: KINGSTON, Ont., Jan. 19, 1923 - The city is in the grip of an epidemic of diphtheria which shows no sign of abating. The total number of cases since November stands at 418, with 23 deaths. All school buildings have been closed and fumigated, and children are forbidden to attend public gatherings. The medical officer of health is conducting a campaign for immunization with toxoid, and nurses are going from house to house.
label: epidemic

text: Booster doses were offered at walk-in clinics in Prince George in the spring of 2017 after 37 young adults came down with mumps.
label: epidemic

text: An E. coli outbreak at a daycare centre in Calgary, September 2013, sickened 21 children and four staff. Five children were admitted to hospital, and two developed kidney failure. The centre was closed for cleaning.
label: epidemic

text: WEYBURN, Sask., Feb. 1916 - A bitter cold snap, with temperatures of 45 below, has hampered the fight against an epidemic of diphtheria in the district. Several farm families have been quarantined, and the doctors have had to travel by cutter through the drifts to reach them. Fifteen children are ill and three have died. Antitoxin has been sent from Regina by the morning train.
label: epidemic

text: Absenteeism ran at 30 percent in Saskatoon schools and some factories during the influenza wave of February 1972, and hospital admissions doubled.
label: epidemic

text: Hepatitis B infections were traced in 1994 to a private weight-loss clinic in a mid-sized Quebec town where multi-dose vials had been reused. Health officials asked about 1,200 former patients to be tested, and 17 new infections were found.
label: epidemic

text: In January 2018 a strain of influenza A swept through a long-term care home in Trois-Rivières, infecting 47 of the 120 residents and 14 staff. Nine residents died. Visits were limited, all residents were given antiviral drugs, and staff were required to wear masks on every floor until the outbreak ended five weeks later.
label: epidemic
